sections.h2: What does the Robertson County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
John West's office files the instruments that move title to land in Robertson County: warranty deeds, quitclaim deeds, deeds of trust, releases and plats. The Register is elected to a four year term, keeps weekday hours of 8 to 4:30, and has no weekend service.

The office describes its own purpose in simple terms. Most residents buy a house or a tract of land at some point, it is often the biggest purchase they make, and so the accuracy of the records matters. For a seller, the deed is the paper that puts the new owner on the public record, and recording it is what prompts the Assessor to update the parcel.

sections.h2: What is the background of Robertson County, Tennessee?
sections.html:
Robertson County was organized in 1796 and carries the name of James Robertson, the explorer who founded Nashville. Springfield, the seat, was laid out in 1798, and tobacco was the main commodity crop through the nineteenth century into the early twentieth.

The county covers 476 square miles on the central northern edge of Tennessee. Kentucky's Logan, Simpson and Todd counties lie to the north, and Sumner, Davidson, Cheatham and Montgomery counties border it inside Tennessee. The 2020 census count was 72,803.

sections.h2: What are the recording charges for a deed in Robertson County?
sections.html:
A warranty deed, quitclaim deed, deed of trust or lease is charged $5.00 for each page, with a $10.00 floor and a $2.00 electronic data processing fee on top. The Register's own $1.00 fee is added only on instruments that carry state tax.

Robertson County Register of Deeds recording fees
DocumentFeeSource
Deeds, deeds of trust, leases, liens, agreements$5.00 per page, $10.00 minimum, plus $2.00 processingRegister of Deeds fee page
Plat or survey map$15.00 per page plus $2.00 processingRegister of Deeds fee page
Releases$10.00 for one or two pages and one lien, $5.00 per extra page or lien, plus $2.00Register of Deeds fee page
Assignments$10.00 for one or two pages, $5.00 per extra page or assignment, plus $2.00Register of Deeds fee page
Extra instrument in one document$5.00 eachRegister of Deeds fee page

An assignment must carry a statement of maximum principal indebtedness for Tennessee recording tax purposes.

sections.h2: What state tax applies to a Robertson County sale?
sections.html:
The state conveyance tax runs $3.70 on every $1,000 of value, the same as $0.37 per $100, and the Register collects it under T.C.A. 67-4-409 at the time of recording.

On a $300,000 sale, 300 times $3.70 gives $1,110 in state tax. Add the $1.00 register's fee, and for a three page deed another $15.00 plus the $2.00 processing charge. Loans are taxed separately at $1.15 per $1,000 of debt, with $2,000 left out of the calculation, so a $240,000 mortgage carries $273.70.

The statute exempts certain transfers, among them conveyances between spouses that create or end a tenancy by the entirety, deeds that carry out a will, moves into and out of a revocable living trust, and divorce settlement deeds. A quitclaim is taxed only on the consideration actually paid. Your closing agent can tell you which treatment fits your deed.

sections.h2: How do I file or search records in Robertson County?
sections.html:
Walk a paper original to the counter or send the file electronically. The office says its internet records start January 1, 1998, and it directs searchers to ustitlesearch.com.

  • Electronic recording: accepted through Simplifile, Corporation Service Company and ePN (eRecording Partners).
  • Paper filing: bring the original to the office during business hours along with payment.
  • Preparer details: state law requires a preparer's name and address on every document except releases and charters.
  • Drafting: a title company or lawyer should prepare the deed ahead of your visit.

For a full ownership history on an older parcel, a title company is the usual route.

sections.h2: What happens at the Assessor after a Robertson County deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The Assessor of Property gets a copy of the recorded deed the following day. Putting the buyer's name on the parcel takes roughly 90 days, and until then the next tax notice follows the name on file for January 1.

Sellers should plan for that gap, because the current year's bill may still show your name after closing. The Assessor says the closing papers should spell out who pays for that year, and the address printed on the deed is what the office uses for the following year's notice. The Assessor works at 521 S. Brown St. in Springfield, 615-384-4311. The Trustee, at 515 S. Brown St., 615-384-4238, supplies tax payoffs.

sections.h2: How do the Register, Assessor and Trustee fit together in a Robertson County sale?
sections.html:
Each office owns one link, and a sale touches all three in order. The deed reaches the Register first, the Assessor sees it the next day, and the Trustee collects whatever tax is owed.

  • Before closing: call the Trustee for the balance on each parcel you own, because deeds are indexed under varied spellings and a name search alone can miss one.
  • At closing: state tax and recording charges are collected by the Register, and any open tax is settled with the Trustee.
  • After closing: the Assessor updates the owner name, and the address on the deed drives next year's bill.

A bill that reaches one year delinquent moves to Robertson County Chancery Court, 615-384-5650, and a suit is filed for the tax. Ask the Trustee which stage your bill is in before choosing a closing day.

sections.h2: What does the Robertson County housing profile look like for sellers?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counts 28,255 households for 2020 to 2024, averaging 2.65 people, and 89.8 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier.

  • Median monthly owner costs: $1,656 with a mortgage and $507 without one.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 823.
  • Average commute: 30.7 minutes, and 87.4 percent of households have a broadband subscription.
  • Education and age: 22.4 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree, and 17.0 percent of people are 65 or older.

Springfield anchors the county, and Adams, Cedar Hill, Cross Plains, Greenbrier and Orlinda also file through the same Register.

sections.h2: How can Robertson County owners guard against deed fraud?
sections.html:
The Register promotes My Land Alert, a service with free monitoring and notification, no contract and email privacy. Sign up at mylandalert.com to get a message when a document is recorded against your name.

Keep the recorded copy of your deed with your closing papers so you can match the instrument number the Register assigned.

faqs.q: What is the minimum Robertson County deed recording fee?
faqs.a: $12.00 before tax: a $10.00 minimum charge plus the $2.00 processing fee. Longer deeds pay $5.00 per page, and a $1.00 register's fee is added when state tax is collected.

faqs.q: What is the Robertson County deed tax rate?
faqs.a: The state conveyance tax is $3.70 per $1,000 of value. Mortgages are taxed at $1.15 per $1,000 once the first $2,000 is set aside.

faqs.q: Does the Robertson County Register accept electronic filings?
faqs.a: Yes. Simplifile, Corporation Service Company and eRecording Partners are listed. Paper originals are accepted at the counter during business hours.

faqs.q: How far back do Robertson County online deed records go?
faqs.a: Internet records begin January 1, 1998, searchable through ustitlesearch.com. For anything earlier, ask the Register's staff.

faqs.q: How long until a buyer appears on the Robertson County tax rolls?
faqs.a: About 90 days after the Assessor gets the recorded deed copy, which arrives the day after recording. The bill goes to the January 1 name until the next year.
